1.he: נָסַעְתִּי מֵאֶרֶץ נוֹף. אֶל יְפֵה נוֹף
1.note: Noph is Memphis (Isa 19:13), that is, Egypt. The rhyme plays on נוֹף twice: "the land of Noph" and "fair in situation" (יְפֵה נוֹף, Ps 48:3, said of Mount Zion).

2.he: עַל הַיְלָדִים צָלְחָה רוּחָהּ וְטֶרֶם יִקְרְאוּ אֶל הַנְּבוּאָה עָנְתָה
2.note: Perhaps alludes to b. Bava Batra 12b, that since the Temple was destroyed prophecy was given to fools and children. The reading of the line is uncertain.

3.note: The line begins and ends with the same word יָפְתָה ("she is fair"), a play kept in the English.

4.note: The source prints קְרָבַי ("my inward parts") in brackets after לִבִּי, a variant reading. The sense is the same.

5.note: The sotah, the wife suspected of adultery, who drinks the bitter waters (Num 5:11-31). These verses apply the ordeal to Zion.

6.he: שְׁנוֹת אֶלֶף וְעוֹד מֵאָה וְאַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה
6.note: 1,148 years after the destruction of the Second Temple (70 CE), that is, about 1218 CE, the time of al-Ḥarizi's visit.

7.note: The same word twice: "her soul pined until it was spent" (compare Ps 84:3). A pun on כַּלָּה, "bride", may also be heard.

8.note: The cast-out woman is probably Hagar, driven out (Gen 21:10), with Ishmael, but the speaker has named the sons of Esau as holding the Temple. Who is meant is not clear.

9.he: וְלֹא יוּכָל לְבַכֵּר אֶת בֶּן הָאֲהוּבָה עְל פְּנֵי בֶן הַשְּׂנוּאָה
9.note: Deut 21:16 forbids giving the firstborn's right to the beloved wife's son over the hated wife's firstborn. Here it seems to be God's answer: even if Israel is "hated", it keeps the birthright.

10.he: בִּשְׁנַת אַרְבַּעַת אֲלָפִים וּתְשַׁע מֵאוֹת וַחֲמִשִּׁים לַיְצִירָה
10.note: 4950 of the Creation is 1189/90 CE. Saladin took Jerusalem from the Crusaders in October 1187 (4948).

11.note: In 1 Sam 23:28 סֶלַע הַמַּחְלְקוֹת is usually read "Rock of Escape" (or "of Parting"). Here it is read as "Rock of Divisions", from מַחֲלֹקֶת, strife.
